summary: Ixabepilone is a semisynthetic epothilone B analog microtubule inhibitor used for metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer. It is given in combination with capecitabine after failure of an anthracycline and a taxane, or as monotherapy after failure of an anthracycline, a taxane, and capecitabine. The standard dose is 40 mg/m2 as a 3-hour intravenous infusion every 3 weeks (body surface area capped at 2.2 m2). CRITICAL SAFETY: in combination with capecitabine, ixabepilone is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with AST or ALT greater than 2.5x ULN or bilirubin greater than 1x ULN because of a markedly increased risk of toxicity and neutropenia-related death. Key toxicities include myelosuppression, peripheral neuropathy, and hypersensitivity reactions (it is formulated in Cremophor EL).
indications: Metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer in combination with capecitabine after failure of an anthracycline and a taxane
Metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer as monotherapy after failure of an anthracycline, a taxane, and capecitabine

dosage.d: 40 mg/m2 over 3 hours every 3 weeks; doses for body surface area greater than 2.2 m2 should be calculated based on 2.2 m2
Reduce in increments (e.g., to 32 mg/m2, then 25 mg/m2) for neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, or grade 3+ neuropathy per labeling
dosage.n: Hold/reduce per blood counts and neuropathy

dosage.d: Reduced starting doses (e.g., 32 mg/m2 or 20-30 mg/m2) depending on degree of AST/ALT and bilirubin elevation per labeling
CONTRAINDICATED if AST or ALT greater than 2.5x ULN or bilirubin greater than 1x ULN

admin: Premedicate approximately 1 hour before infusion with an H1 antagonist (e.g., diphenhydramine) and an H2 antagonist (e.g., ranitidine) to reduce hypersensitivity
For patients with a prior hypersensitivity reaction, add corticosteroid premedication and extend the infusion time
Administer as a 3-hour intravenous infusion using DEHP-free administration set with a 0.2-1.2 micron in-line filter
Reconstitute and dilute only with the supplied diluent and approved infusion solutions per labeling; complete infusion within the stability window
Use cytotoxic handling and disposal precautions; monitor for hypersensitivity during the infusion
moa: Ixabepilone is a semisynthetic analog of epothilone B that binds directly to beta-tubulin subunits on microtubules. It suppresses the dynamic instability of microtubules - stabilizing them and promoting tubulin polymerization - which blocks cells in the mitotic (M) phase of the cell-division cycle and leads to apoptotic cell death. Unlike taxanes, it binds preferentially to certain beta-tubulin isotypes and retains activity against tumor cells that overexpress P-glycoprotein, multidrug-resistance proteins, or beta-III tubulin, accounting for activity in some taxane-resistant cancers.

absolute: Combination with capecitabine in patients with AST or ALT greater than 2.5x ULN or bilirubin greater than 1x ULN (risk of toxicity and neutropenia-related death)
History of severe (grade 3/4) hypersensitivity reaction to drugs containing Cremophor EL (polyoxyethylated castor oil)
Baseline neutrophil count less than 1500 cells/mm3 or platelet count less than 100,000 cells/mm3
relative: Pre-existing moderate to severe peripheral neuropathy
Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (alter exposure)
monitor: Complete blood count before each cycle and as indicated
Hepatic function (AST, ALT, bilirubin) before each cycle, especially with capecitabine

preg: Ixabepilone can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman, based on its mechanism and animal data. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose. If used in pregnancy or if the patient becomes pregnant, advise of the potential hazard to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether ixabepilone is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in milk and because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, breastfeeding should be discontinued during treatment.
renal: Ixabepilone has not been studied in patients with severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease; it is minimally renally excreted, and no specific dose adjustment is provided for renal impairment in the labeling. Use caution and monitor.
hepatic: Hepatic impairment increases exposure and toxicity. Monotherapy requires reduced starting doses based on the degree of AST/ALT and bilirubin elevation. In COMBINATION with capecitabine, ixabepilone is CONTRAINDICATED when AST or ALT is greater than 2.5x ULN or bilirubin is greater than 1x ULN because of the risk of severe toxicity and neutropenia-related death.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, etc.) - increase ixabepilone exposure and toxicity; avoid or reduce dose
Capecitabine in hepatic impairment - contraindicated due to fatal neutropenia risk
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St John's wort) - decrease exposure and efficacy; avoid
Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy or radiation - additive bone-marrow suppression
minor: Drugs that prolong QT or affect cardiac conduction - monitor in patients with cardiac risk
interactions.food: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibitors) may increase ixabepilone levels - avoid.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol due to additive hepatotoxicity and central effects in patients with neuropathy and marrow suppression.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC and liver function tests (AST, ALT, bilirubin) before each cycle to guide dosing and detect contraindications.

serious: Severe myelosuppression and febrile neutropenia (neutropenia-related death, especially with capecitabine in hepatic impairment)
Cardiac adverse reactions (myocardial ischemia, ventricular dysfunction)

monitoring: Complete blood count before each cycle; hold or reduce dose for neutropenia/thrombocytopenia
Liver function tests (AST, ALT, bilirubin) before therapy and each cycle - critical before any capecitabine combination
Peripheral neuropathy assessment at each visit
Vital signs and hypersensitivity during infusion
Cardiac symptoms in patients with underlying cardiac disease
counsel: Report numbness, tingling, burning, or weakness in your hands or feet promptly - these can be signs of nerve damage
Call right away for fever, chills, sore throat, or signs of infection (your white-cell count may be low)
Tell the team immediately during the infusion if you feel flushing, rash, itching, or trouble breathing
Use effective birth control during treatment and for 7 months after; do not breastfeed
Avoid grapefruit, certain antifungal/antibiotic drugs, and alcohol unless cleared by your oncologist
pk: Cytotoxic effect over days; clinical response assessed across cycles
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C (36-46 F); protect from light; bring to room temperature before reconstitution and use diluted solution within the labeled stability window
pearls: CRITICAL: with capecitabine, contraindicated if AST or ALT greater than 2.5x ULN or bilirubin greater than 1x ULN - associated with toxicity and neutropenia-related DEATH; always check LFTs first
Formulated in Cremophor EL (polyoxyethylated castor oil) - premedicate with H1 and H2 antagonists; add steroids and slow the infusion after any prior reaction
Retains activity in some taxane-resistant tumors (poor substrate for P-glycoprotein/MDR efflux)
Peripheral neuropathy is cumulative and dose-limiting - dose-reduce or discontinue for grade 3 or higher
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers and grapefruit significantly alter exposure - review concomitant drugs and diet
missed: Ixabepilone is administered in a supervised oncology setting on a 3-week cycle. There is no patient self-administered missed dose; if a scheduled infusion is delayed, the oncology team reschedules based on blood counts, neuropathy, and hepatic function, and may adjust the dose accordingly.
overdose: There is no known antidote for ixabepilone overdose. Anticipated complications include severe myelosuppression, peripheral neurotoxicity, and gastrointestinal effects. Management is supportive: monitor blood counts, provide growth-factor and infection support as needed, and treat symptoms; the patient should be observed closely until recovery.
